v.why: Adding a missing input-to-output residual helps much more than swapping an existing conv or pool on edge 3 for skip.
Without the edge-3 shortcut, cutting edge 5 removes a main path into the output node and can nearly disconnect the cell.
When edge 5 is already absent, removing edge 4 leaves node 3 fed only by edge 3, which removes most of the learned computation.
When node 1 does not feed the output directly, removing its input edge loses less, so the harm is smaller.
If edge 2 is none, edge 1 is node 2's only input, so cutting it makes the edge-5 path dead.
If edge 1 is none, edge 2 is node 2's only input, so removing it disconnects node 2 and the edge-5 path.
Swapping the valuable residual skip for a conv hurts, while replacing none or avg_pool with conv tends to help.
Adding a connection where there was none restores information flow, whereas replacing a conv3x3 with skip loses capacity.
Adding a conv where the edge was missing gives a bigger gain than replacing an existing skip or avg_pool.
Without the edge-3 shortcut, a skip on edge 4 supplies a needed residual-like path to the output, so it helps more.
